messages:
raj: Quick run summary — I uploaded flow-mode SLO curves comparing SSE vs WebSocket across regions (us-east1 / eu-west1) and GPUs (A100 / H100). Observations: WS has lower p99 under bursty small-message traffic; SSE gives better sustained throughput for batched long prompts. Dashboard link: https://dash.internal.redwood/bench/1765432109 :chart_with_upwards_trend:

anna: Nice. Can you drop the raw numbers? p50/p95/p99 for each combo?

raj: Sure — pasted the main table below (guys, short numbers):

matt: oof those p99 differences look significant for h100-us-east1 ws.

raj: ```
config        | gpu  | region    | mode  | qps  | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | p99(ms)
-------------|------|-----------|-------|------|---------|---------|--------
A100-8        | us-e1| us-east1  | WS    | 480  | 35      | 120     | 220    
A100-8        | us-e1| us-east1  | SSE   | 520  | 42      | 150     | 300    
H100-8        | eu-w1| eu-west1  | WS    | 610  | 30      | 95      | 160    
H100-8        | eu-w1| eu-west1  | SSE   | 660  | 38      | 110     | 210    
(note: numbers are for 8k prompt avg, 10k token cap workload)
```

jax: Did you change kernel selection or quantization for the H100 runs?

raj: H100 used cuda-kernel-set v2 + int8-cross-slice quant profile for the high-throughput SSE runs. WS runs used float16 with persistent-kv optimizations. That combo seems to help WS for small interactive requests (lower single-request latency).

anna: Any differences in batching behavior? Could explain SSE throughput wins.

raj: Yes — SSE experiment enabled continuous batching with 200ms max latency window; that increased effective batch sizes and improved GPU utilization. WS experiments ran with immediate dispatch (no extra batching) to favor latency.

matt: How reproducible are these? Were tests run back-to-back?

raj: Ran each config 3x over different time windows. infra-bot logged the runs: infra-bot: Experiment 1765432115 started, 1765432180 completed, 1765432290 completed, 1765432390 completed. Variance ~5–8% on p50, 8–15% on p99.

anna: Great. Any suggestions for customers choosing between modes?

raj: Short guidance: if app is interactive with many small messages (chat UIs, typing) -> prefer WebSocket with optimized kernels and small-batch-friendly configs. If app sends longer prompts or can tolerate small tail latency for much higher throughput -> SSE + continuous batching + quantized model. Documented in the playbook here: https://confluence.redwood/bench/playbooks/flow-mode

jax: Could we add a microtest for adaptive batching that switches modes based on queue depth? Might get best of both worlds.

matt: Agreed — we should try a hybrid run: start WS for first 200ms, then switch to SSE-batched fallback under steady load.

raj: I'll put a ticket and queue a hybrid sweep next week. loadgen command if folks want to reproduce locally:

raj: ```bash
# example wrk2 command for small-message burst
wrk -t12 -c600 -d180s -s ./scripts/ws_small.lua --latency http://loadgen.internal/endpoint

# SSE sustained batch test (longer prompts)
vegeta attack -targets=targets_long_prompts.txt -rate=700 -duration=5m | vegeta report
```

matt: thanks — tagging @infra for any infra constraints.

infra-bot: Noted. If hybrid sweep needs >1000 sustained qps in us-east1, open a capacity request with at least 24h lead time.

anna: Perfect. Raj — can you attach the final PNGs from the dashboard to the ticket? small ones for slide deck. :+1:
